description:
Put the real names back into a file you wrote from a pseudonymized document: every tag ([Person 1], or the user's rename such as [Seller]) becomes the original text from the correspondence table. Runs entirely on this machine; nothing is uploaded.

Use it at the end of the anonymize -> work -> re-identify loop: redact_pdf_and_wait with mode "pseudonymize" gave you document_text and correspondence_path; you did the work on the tagged text and wrote the result to a .md, .txt or .docx file, keeping each tag exactly as written, brackets included. Pass that file and correspondence_path here.

It writes "<name>-restored.<ext>" next to your file (never over an existing file) and returns only that path and counts, never a name. Do NOT open, read or quote the restored file or the correspondence CSV: both contain the real names, and reading them puts the personal data into this conversation, which is what pseudonymizing was for. Give the user the path instead.

correspondence_path.description: Absolute path of the correspondence CSV, as returned in correspondence_path by redact_pdf_and_wait or download_correspondence. Pass the path only: do not open the file, it contains the real names.

file_path.description: Absolute path of the file YOU wrote from the pseudonymized text (.md, .markdown, .txt or .docx), with the tags kept as written, e.g. "[Person 1] signed on behalf of [Org 1]". Not the original document.

output_path.description: Where to write the restored copy. Defaults to "<name>-restored.<ext>" next to file_path. Never overwrites an existing file.

name: restore_names
title: Put the real names back into a file written from a pseudonymized document
